name: Kabaddi Raid
subtitle: 3D kabaddi for your phone · Raid, touch and race home
card_blurb: Raid on one breath, touch a defender and race home. Own a franchise or win the Nations Cup.
short_description: Raid, touch and race home in 3D kabaddi. Own a franchise. Win the Nations Cup.
description: Kabaddi Raid is a 3D kabaddi game for your phone. Cross the baulk line on one breath, touch a defender and race back over the midline before they bring you down.
Or defend: read the raid, take him by the ankle, the thigh or the waist, and chain up with a team-mate.
download_size: about 78 MB (Play download per phone, 0.12.3 bundle, per store/PLAY_STORE.md)

features.title: Three ways to play
features.text: Quick Match, a League Season with your own franchise and the player auction, and the Nations Cup.

features.title: Raid and tackle
features.text: Hand and toe touches, kicks, the dubki and the lion jump; ankle, thigh and waist holds and chain tackles.

features.title: The rules as played
features.text: Bonus points, revivals, all outs, do-or-die raids, super tackles and the golden raid, with referees signalling every call.

features.title: Breath or the clock
features.text: Raid on one breath of the cant, or against the 30-second clock: your choice.

features.title: Five grounds
features.text: Twelve franchises, twelve countries and five grounds, from a village mat to a stadium under lights.

features.title: Controls your way
features.text: A stick wherever your thumb lands, a left-handed layout, movable buttons and four levels from Rookie to Legend.

about_sport: Kabaddi is a contact team sport from South Asia, played seven a side. A raider crosses into the other half, touches as many defenders as he can and must get back over the midline before they bring him down, either on one breath while chanting the cant or against a 30-second clock. Defenders score by stopping him: ankle holds, thigh holds, chain tackles.

name: Sepak Takraw Unleashed
subtitle: The kick volleyball of Southeast Asia
card_blurb: The kick volleyball of Southeast Asia: roll spikes, horse-kick serves and blocks at the net.
short_description: Sepak takraw: roll spikes, horse-kick serves and blocks at the net. Real rules.
description: Sepak Takraw Unleashed is sepak takraw for your phone: the kick volleyball of Southeast Asia.
Serve with a foot in the circle, receive with the inside of your foot, set it high by the net, and launch a roll spike over the block.

features.title: The laws as today
features.text: Sets to 15 (win by two, up to 17), best of three, serve alternating every point, three touches a side.

features.title: Every event
features.text: Regu, quadrant, doubles and the team event, for men and women, on a court and net to exact measurements.

features.title: The moves fans know
features.text: Sepak sila, the instep dig, the header, the horse-kick serve, the roll spike, the sunback, the feint and the block.

features.title: Officials and video challenge
features.text: Faults called by the referee, line judges' calls, and a video challenge to overturn them.

features.title: Leagues and internationals
features.text: Club seasons in Malaysian, Thai and Indonesian formats; the World Championship, Royal Cup, Asian and Southeast Asian championships.

features.title: Nothing played for you
features.text: Run your player to the ball with the joystick and kick as the ring closes on it.

about_sport: Sepak takraw is the kick volleyball of Southeast Asia. Players keep a small ball in the air with their feet, knees, chest and head, never their hands, and send it over a net on a badminton-sized court, with at most three touches a side. The main event, the regu, is three a side: the tekong serves from the circle and strikers attack with acrobatic overhead spikes.
disclaimer: Sepak Takraw Unleashed is an independent game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any sepak takraw federation, league, club or player. The clubs' nicknames are invented and the players are fictional; the countries, places and rules are real.

name: Netball Unleashed
subtitle: Netball by the real rules · Seven a side
card_blurb: Netball by the real rules: seven a side, two umpires, 23 nations. Play the whole team or one position.
short_description: Netball by the real rules: lead, pass, defend at 0.9 m, shoot from the circle.
description: Netball Unleashed is netball for your phone, played to the Rules of Netball as they stand today.
Take the centre pass, drive into space, feed the circle and shoot, then win the ball back with an intercept.

features.title: Seven positions, real areas
features.text: GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD and GK, each in her own areas, with bibs on.

features.title: Two umpires, every call
features.text: Footwork, three seconds, obstruction at 0.9 m, contact, offside and over a third, signalled by two umpires.

features.title: Team or one position
features.text: Play the whole team, or pick a bib and play one position all match.

features.title: Three ways to play
features.text: Quick Match with 23 nations, the Nations Cup, and the Club Season: eight clubs and a grand final.

features.title: A box score
features.text: Goals from attempts, feeds, centre pass receives, gains, intercepts, rebounds and penalties for every match.

features.title: Nineteen languages
features.text: From Afrikaans, isiZulu and Kiswahili to Cymraeg, Te Reo Māori, Lea Faka-Tonga and Na Vosa Vakaviti.

about_sport: Netball is a fast passing game, seven a side, played most in Australia, New Zealand, the UK, southern Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific. Players may not run with the ball or hold it for more than three seconds, each position keeps to its own areas of the court, and only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack can score, from inside the circle.
disclaimer: Netball Unleashed is an independent game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any netball governing body, league, club or player. The players are fictional; the countries and the rules are real.

name: Kho Kho Rush
subtitle: The chasing game of India
card_blurb: The chasing game of India: sit in the lane, give the kho, chase and pole dive. Two rule books.
short_description: Kho kho to the real rules: sit in the lane, give the kho, chase and pole dive.
description: Kho Kho Rush is kho kho for your phone: the chasing game of India.
Sit in the lane with your side, rise on a kho, chase the defenders to the pole, and dive to touch them out before the turn runs down.

features.title: Two rule books
features.text: Classic, nine a side as the national championships play it; Fast, seven a side from the 2025 world championship.

features.title: Every chaser rule
features.text: Keep your direction, never cross the central lane, turn only round a pole, and give the kho from behind.

features.title: Touch, sky dive, pole dive
features.text: Defenders on in batches of three. Out by a touch, a sky dive, a pole dive or a late entry.

features.title: Umpires on both lines
features.text: Umpires on both side lines whistle a foul until it is put right, with a referee and a timekeeper.

features.title: Championships and City League
features.text: Sixteen nations or sixteen states, men's and women's, or eight invented city sides home and away.

features.title: Four grounds
features.text: A village ground at dusk, a school ground in the morning, an indoor arena on mats, a floodlit stadium.

about_sport: Kho kho is a traditional chasing game from India. The chasing side sits in a line of squares down the middle of the field, with a pole at each end, while one active chaser runs after the defenders. He may not cross the central lane or turn back, so he hands on the chase by touching a seated team-mate from behind and calling "kho".
disclaimer: Kho Kho Rush is an independent game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any kho kho federation, league, club or player. The players are fictional; the countries, states and rules are real.

name: Hurling Heroes
subtitle: Ireland's ancient field sport · Iománaíocht
card_blurb: Ireland's ancient field sport, fifteen a side, to the 2026 rules. In English or Irish.
short_description: Hurling, Ireland's ancient field sport: fifteen a side, the real rules.
description: Hurling Heroes is hurling for your phone, Ireland's ancient field sport: the clash of the ash, fifteen a side, goals and points.
Play on a parish field at dusk or in front of a full stadium. Lift the sliotar, solo through, and strike it over the bar.

offline.note: Listing: "Plays offline (only the optional HD download uses the internet)."

permissions: android.permission.INTERNET (only for the optional HD pack download)

features.title: The 2026 playing rules
features.text: Two halves of 35 minutes, a goal worth three points, puck-outs, frees, 65s, sideline cuts and penalties.

features.title: Solo and strike
features.text: Four steps with the sliotar in your hand, then solo it on your hurley.

features.title: Every official on the field
features.text: The referee whistles and shows cards; linesmen flag sideline cuts; umpires wave white for a point, green for a goal.

features.title: The Summer Championship
features.text: Two groups of five, then knock-outs to the final; the other ten counties play the Tier Two Cup.

features.title: As Gaeilge
features.text: English or Irish, with the game's own Irish terms: camán, sliotar, cúl, cúilín, poc amach.

features.title: Graphics for your phone
features.text: Low, Medium and High, changed any time, plus an optional HD download for recent high-end phones.

about_sport: Hurling is Ireland's ancient field sport, played fifteen a side. Players carry an ash stick, the hurley (camán), and a small leather ball, the sliotar, which can be caught, balanced on the stick while running, or struck the length of the field. A goal under the bar is worth three points; a point goes over the bar between the posts.
disclaimer: Hurling Heroes is an independent game. It is not connected with or endorsed by any sporting body, county board or club. The counties appear by their place names, in colours of the game's own design; every player is invented.

name: Floorball Unleashed
subtitle: The fast indoor stick game · Five and a goalkeeper a side
card_blurb: The fast indoor stick game: five and a goalkeeper a side, to the 2026 international rules.
short_description: Floorball five a side with goalkeepers, to the real rules. Shoot, pass, score!
description: Floorball Unleashed is floorball for your phone: the fast indoor stick game of Sweden, Finland, Switzerland and Czechia.
Five and a goalkeeper a side on a 40 by 20 metre rink inside the boards, to floorball's international Rules of the Game in force from 1 July 2026.

features.title: The 2026 rules
features.text: Three periods, face-offs, hit-ins and free-hits, the goalkeeper area, two- and five-minute penalties, power plays and penalty shots.

features.title: Two referees
features.text: Two referees who whistle and signal every call: free-hit, advantage, delayed penalty, two minutes, passive play, goal.

features.title: Pull the goalkeeper
features.text: Late in a match the team behind pulls its goalkeeper for a sixth outfield player.

features.title: Teams that play floorball
features.text: A 2-1-2 defence, flying line changes every fifty seconds, wingers wide and the centre in the slot.

features.title: World Finals and club season
features.text: Sixteen nations at the World Finals, or ten clubs in a league with 3-2-1-0 points and a final.

features.title: A box score
features.text: Shots on goal, saves, penalty minutes, power-play goals, every goal and every penalty with its rule.

about_sport: Floorball is a fast indoor stick game, played most in Sweden, Finland, Switzerland and Czechia. Each side has five outfield players and a goalkeeper, on a 40 by 20 metre rink inside low boards. Outfield players use light plastic sticks and a plastic ball with holes; the goalkeeper plays without a stick.
disclaimer: Floorball Unleashed is an independent game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any floorball federation, league, club or player. The players are fictional; the countries and the rules are real.

name: Pok Ta Pok Rivals
subtitle: The hip ballgame of Mexico · Ulama de cadera
card_blurb: The Mesoamerican hip ballgame: ulama from Sinaloa and the stone courts of the Yucatán.
short_description: The hip ballgame of Mexico: ulama, the heavy rubber ball, the count to eight.
description: Pok Ta Pok Rivals is the Mesoamerican ballgame on your phone, played as it is still played today.
Strike a heavy rubber ball with your hip across the analco of a long earth court, read its low bounce, dive for it as it skids along the ground, and drive it past the other town's end.

offline.note: The listing does not say "plays offline"; store/PLAY_STORE.md: "one permission (vibration) and no internet access"; Play tags include Offline (store/PLAY_CONSOLE_ANSWERS.md).

features.title: Ulama de cadera
features.text: The game still played in southern Sinaloa: four or five a side on a strip of packed earth.

features.title: The hip only
features.text: Touch the ball with anything else and the raya goes to the other side.

features.title: The real count
features.text: Rayas go up and down, and in urria a whole count can be wiped out. First to eight.

features.title: The classic stone court
features.text: An I-shaped court rebuilt from the old chronicles, with a stone ring that wins the game outright.

features.title: Four courts, sixteen towns
features.text: Towns from Sinaloa, the Yucatán, Quintana Roo, Chiapas, Guatemala, Belize and Honduras, each with its own colors.

features.title: Team or one player
features.text: Play as the whole team, or be one player for the whole match.

about_sport: The Mesoamerican ballgame is more than 3,000 years old. Its living form, ulama de cadera, is still played in villages of southern Sinaloa, Mexico: two sides strike a heavy rubber ball with the hip only along a long strip of packed earth, while judges called veedores keep the count. In the Yucatán and Central America, teams have revived pelota maya on stone courts.
disclaimer: Pok Ta Pok Rivals is an independent game, not connected with or endorsed by any sporting body, federation, tournament or club. Towns appear by their place names only; every player is invented.
